selection.reason: The bounded quotient lemma formalizes both clauses of the p.160 unit under the source's locally factorial hypothesis: the multiplicative quotient is the sheaf of locally principal divisor germs, and factorial local rings identify these with Weil-divisor germs.

hypotheses: X is a Noetherian integral scheme
Every local ring of X is a unique factorization domain for the Weil-divisor identification
K_X and O_X^* are used multiplicatively and the quotient is taken in sheaves of abelian groups
claims: Without factoriality, the quotient stalks are the germs of locally principal divisors represented by meromorphic functions modulo local units
Under local factoriality, the divisor map induces K_X^*/O_X^* isomorphic to the Weil-divisor sheaf D_X
At each UFD stalk the quotient is K^*/A^* and records the height-one valuation exponents
mathematical_scope.boundary: The general locally-principal quotient is stated via meromorphic representatives modulo local units; the Weil-divisor identification is conditional on local UFDs. No analytic quotient, GAGA comparison, descent, projective-bundle lifting, or whole-section completion claim is made.

mapping_projection.rationale: The new lemma gives the p.160 quotient-as-locally-principal-germs statement and, under factorial local rings, its identification with the Weil-divisor sheaf. It reuses the already proved locally-UFD exact sequence and does not conflate the p.161 cohomology successor or the analytic lifting boundary.

gap_projection.reason: The exact bounded algebraic p.160 unit is now represented; analytic or later lifting claims remain separate.
